title: The crowd model family: choosing the right tool
summary: Hydraulic calculations, macroscopic, cellular, force-based, velocity-based, step-based and heuristic models each answer different questions. Choose by the question, the scale and the data you have.
outcomes: place each model family on a scale from hand calculation to cognitive model
match a model family to a research or design question
know which open simulators implement which models
narration_en: You now know three ways to model a crowd: as a fluid, as people hopping on a grid, and as particles pushed by forces. There are more. Velocity-based models choose a speed and direction directly, for example the collision-free speed model, where each person walks as fast as possible without colliding within a short time horizon. The optimal steps model, developed by Seitz and Köster, moves people in discrete steps, choosing the best point on a circle around them. Cognitive heuristic models, from Moussaïd, Helbing and Theraulaz, assume people look ahead and head where they can walk furthest towards their goal without a collision. At the other end of the scale, the hydraulic method is a hand calculation with flow rates and walking speeds, still used in building codes. No model is best for everything. The question decides: sizing an exit, forecasting a city-wide event, studying pushing at a door, or exploring how individual decisions shape a crowd. Open simulators such as JuPedSim and Vadere implement several of these models, so you can compare them on the same scenario.
narration_ar: تعرف الآن ثلاث طرق لنمذجة الحشد: كسائل، وكأشخاص يقفزون على شبكة، وكجسيمات تدفعها قوى. وهناك المزيد. فالنماذج القائمة على السرعة تختار السرعة والاتجاه مباشرة، كنموذج السرعة الخالية من التصادم، حيث يمشي كل شخص بأقصى سرعة ممكنة دون أن يصطدم خلال أفق زمني قصير. ونموذج الخطوات المثلى، الذي طوّره زايتس وكوستر، يحرّك الناس بخطوات منفصلة، مختاراً أفضل نقطة على دائرة حولهم. ونماذج الاستدلال المعرفي، من موسعيد وهيلبنغ وثيرولاز، تفترض أن الناس ينظرون أمامهم ويتجهون حيث يستطيعون المشي أبعد مسافة نحو هدفهم دون تصادم. وفي الطرف الآخر من السلم، الطريقة الهيدروليكية حساب يدوي بمعدلات التدفق وسرعات المشي، وما زالت تُستخدم في أنظمة البناء. لا يوجد نموذج هو الأفضل لكل شيء. السؤال هو الذي يقرر: تحديد عرض مخرج، أو التنبؤ بفعالية على مستوى مدينة، أو دراسة التدافع عند باب، أو استكشاف كيف تشكّل القرارات الفردية الحشد. وتطبّق محاكيات مفتوحة مثل JuPedSim وVadere عدة نماذج من هذه، فتستطيع مقارنتها على السيناريو نفسه.

diagram.title: From hand calculation to cognition
diagram.caption: Model families ordered by detail. More detail means more realism in some respects, more parameters and more computing.

nodes.label: Hydraulic
nodes.detail: Egress time from flow rates and walking speeds (SFPE Handbook, PD 7974-6, Green Guide). Transparent, fast, no behaviour.

nodes.label: Macroscopic
nodes.detail: Continuum or cell-transmission models (module 2.2). Large networks, real-time forecasts.

nodes.label: Cellular automata
nodes.detail: Floor-field CAs (module 2.3). Fast, discrete, need calibration.

nodes.label: Force-based
nodes.detail: Social force and variants (module 2.4). Contact, clogging, pushing.

nodes.label: Velocity-based
nodes.detail: Speed and direction chosen directly to avoid collisions, e.g. the collision-free speed model (Tordeux, Chraibi and Seyfried 2016) or ORCA.

nodes.label: Optimal steps
nodes.detail: Discrete steps to the best point on a circle (Seitz and Köster 2012), implemented in Vadere.

nodes.label: Cognitive heuristics
nodes.detail: Visual heuristics: head for the direction with the longest free walk towards the goal; keep a time gap (Moussaïd, Helbing and Theraulaz 2011).

nodes.label: Your question
nodes.detail: Scale, phenomenon, data available, time and the need to explain results to decision makers.

tour.text: At one end, a hand calculation with flow rates: transparent and quick.
Then macroscopic fields, grid hops and forces: more detail, more parameters.
Velocity and step models choose speeds or steps directly to avoid collisions.
Cognitive heuristics model what people see and decide.
Your question decides which family to use.

sections.heading: Seven families
sections.html: From simplest to most detailed: hydraulic calculations; macroscopic (continuum and cell-transmission) models; cellular automata; force-based models; velocity-based models; optimal steps; cognitive heuristics. The model atlas has an animation, a simulator and a mind map for each.

sections.heading: Velocity-based and step-based models
sections.html:
The collision-free speed model (Tordeux, Chraibi and Seyfried 2016) sets each person's speed to the largest value that avoids a collision within a time gap T:

v = min( v0, max(0, (s − ℓ) ÷ T) )

where s is the distance to the person ahead and ℓ the body length. It reproduces the fundamental diagram with few parameters. The optimal steps model (Seitz and Köster 2012) moves people in steps to the best point on a circle, scoring distance to the goal and personal space.

sections.heading: Cognitive heuristics
sections.html: Moussaïd, Helbing and Theraulaz (2011) proposed two rules: (1) walk in the direction that gets you closest to your goal before you would collide with someone, scanning your field of vision; (2) walk at a speed that keeps a time gap τ to the first obstacle. Adding body contact forces, the same rules reproduce lanes, stop-and-go waves and turbulence at high density.

sections.heading: Choosing by the question
sections.html: Ask: what scale (a door, a building, a city)? Which phenomenon (capacity, queues, pushing, behaviour)? Which data can calibrate it? How will decision makers understand it? For a code check, a hydraulic calculation may be right; for a city festival network, a macroscopic or CA model; for pushing at a gate, a force-based model; for how information changes behaviour, a cognitive or agent-based model with route choice.

takeaways: Seven model families run from hand calculations to cognitive heuristics.
Velocity-based models choose a collision-free speed directly; optimal steps moves people in discrete steps.
Cognitive heuristics model what people see and decide.
Choose by scale, phenomenon, available data and audience; open simulators let you compare.

glossary.def: Egress calculation using flow rates and speeds, without individual behaviour.
A model in which agents choose their velocity directly, usually to avoid collisions.
Speed = min(v₀, (gap − body length)/T) (Tordeux, Chraibi and Seyfried 2016).
Agents move in discrete steps to the best point on a circle (Seitz and Köster 2012).
Simple perception-based rules for direction and speed (Moussaïd et al. 2011).
